images.caption:
All done quietly and well, top marks to the Tesco staff and to the Prestwich public.

I had intended to photograph the empty shelves...but that was last week, everything was near normal today.

images.caption:
It's a week since my last shopping trip, I am out of food and I need to pick up a prescription, also.

Not much activity in Prestwich: library closed (centre of pic), so too most of the shops; car park almost empty. Weird.
images.alt:
It's a week since my last shopping trip, I am out of food and I need to pick up a prescription, also.

images.caption: The people in the picture are in the queue for Iceland, two metres apart, enter one at a time.
images.alt: The people in the picture are in the queue for Iceland, two metres apart, enter one at a time.

images.caption:
The queue at Tesco's went halfway round the car park, but as the people were two or three metres apart there were only about fifty of us in it, and I was inside in ten minutes. Almost there, now.
Lots of cheerfulness and good humour, from the would-be customers and from those who were marshalling the queue.

Quite warm and not raining, thankfully.

images.caption:
Four buses in the Museum of Transport in Manchester, all in their original liveries. From left to right, they are:
North Western Road Car Company's 432 (AJA 152), a 1939 Bristol K5G/Willowbrook.
Manchester Corporation's 3496 (TNA496), a 1958 Leyland Titan PD2/Burlingham.
Manchester Corporation's 4632 (4632 VM), a 1963 Daimler CVG6/Metro Cammell.
Salford Corporation's 112 (TRJ 112), a 1962 Daimler CVG6/Metro Cammell.
